Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. The tiger is actually a big part of many South Asian countries and even culture. The bengal tiger specifically is native to Bangladesh , Nepal, India and Bhutan and holds significance and the royal bengal tiger is Bangladesh’s national animal, along with the tiger also being significant to Tamil people as a symbol of liberation with use dating back to the chola empire (modern day south India & Sri Lanka).
